mil5.2.2:0.4: 2. Question on What Is Not to Be Answered
mil5.2.2:1.1: “Venerable Nāgasena, this too was said by the Blessed One:
mil5.2.2:1.2: ‘Ānanda, the Tathāgata has no closed fist of a teacher with regard to the teachings.’ And yet when the elder Māluṅkyaputta put a question to him, he did not answer.
mil5.2.2:1.3: This question, Venerable Nāgasena, will be one-sided on either horn: either it was through not knowing, or through concealing it.
mil5.2.2:1.4: If, Venerable Nāgasena, the Blessed One said
mil5.2.2:1.5: ‘The Tathāgata has no closed fist of a teacher with regard to the teachings,’ then he did not answer the elder Māluṅkyaputta because he did not know.
mil5.2.2:1.6: But if he did not answer while knowing, then the Tathāgata does have a closed fist of a teacher with regard to the teachings.
mil5.2.2:1.7: This too is a two-horned dilemma that has been put to you for you to resolve.”
mil5.2.2:2.1: “Your majesty, the Blessed One did say ‘Ānanda, the Tathāgata has no closed fist of a teacher with regard to the teachings,’ and the question put by the elder Māluṅkyaputta did go unanswered. But that was neither through not knowing nor through concealing it.
mil5.2.2:2.2: There are four ways of answering a question, your majesty.
mil5.2.2:2.4: A question to be answered categorically; a question to be answered by analysis; a question to be answered by counter-questioning; and a question to be set aside.
mil5.2.2:3.1: And what, your majesty, is a question to be answered categorically?
mil5.2.2:3.2: ‘Is form impermanent’: this is a question to be answered categorically.
mil5.2.2:3.6: ‘Is consciousness impermanent’: this is a question to be answered categorically. These are questions to be answered categorically.
mil5.2.2:4.1: What is a question to be answered by analysis?
mil5.2.2:4.2: ‘Is form, thus, impermanent?’ is a question to be answered by analysis.
mil5.2.2:4.6: ‘Is consciousness, thus, impermanent?’: this is a question to be answered by analysis. These are questions to be answered by analysis.
mil5.2.2:5.1: What is a question to be answered by counter-questioning?
mil5.2.2:5.2: ‘Does one cognize everything with the eye?’ This is a question to be answered by counter-questioning.
mil5.2.2:6.1: What is a question to be set aside?
mil5.2.2:6.6: ‘is the world both finite and infinite’;
mil5.2.2:6.7: ‘is the world neither finite nor infinite’;
mil5.2.2:6.8: ‘are the soul and the body the same’;
mil5.2.2:6.9: ‘is the soul one thing and the body another’;
mil5.2.2:6.11: ‘does the Tathāgata not exist after death’;
mil5.2.2:6.12: ‘does the Tathāgata both exist and not exist after death’;
mil5.2.2:6.13: ‘does the Tathāgata neither exist nor not exist after death’: this is a question to be set aside.
mil5.2.2:6.14: These are questions to be set aside.
mil5.2.2:7.1: The Blessed One, your majesty, did not answer the elder Māluṅkyaputta’s question because it was one to be set aside.
mil5.2.2:7.2: And why should that question be set aside?
mil5.2.2:7.3: There is no cause or reason that would serve to explain it; therefore it is to be set aside.
mil5.2.2:7.4: For the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, there is no uttering of speech without cause and without reason.”
mil5.2.2:7.5: “Well said, Venerable Nāgasena. I accept it as you say.”
